problems.description: 73 convention violations (score 0.49): functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE across new files like build-stats.ts and cache-manager.ts — a regression from the deleted seed, which was conventionally clean.
34.3% duplication across the new source — high copy-paste in a greenfield ~700-line codebase (excluding package-lock), which will make future sessions harder to modify coherently.
Cognitive complexity +39 with 8 new code smells in a single session — the new module structure already carries nontrivial conditional nesting/indirection that will resist refactoring.

Wholesale deletion of the 106-line seed (index.ts) rather than building on/replacing it incrementally; acceptable for a greenfield session, but the mismatch (todo API seed removed in favor of an 'ssg' project) should be called out — flagging in case it was unintentional.
Committed 3656-line package-lock.json (fine practice) but the old express/better-sqlite3 deps vanish silently with no explanation in the commit message.

strengths: Test harness added up front (jest.config.js with ts-jest, testMatch patterns), indicating a testable design intent.
SonarQube reports 0 new bugs — no correctness regressions introduced.
Scope is contained (9 files; ~700 real source lines beyond the lockfile) for a session-1 scaffold.
commit_reviews.summary: A conventionally clean but buggy seed was replaced with a functional SSG scaffold that ships tests and no new bugs, but the low convention score (0.49 / 73 violations), 34.3% duplication, and +8 smells make this session a net regression on architecture and convention adherence.

problems.description: @types/chokidar@2.1.7 is a deprecated stub types package — chokidar v3 (installed as ^3.6.0) ships its own TypeScript definitions. Installing the stub adds a version-mismatched (types v2 for runtime v3) dependency that the registry itself deprecates.
Convention score 0.49 with 73 violations concentrated in build-stats.ts and cache-manager.ts: functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE.

331 added lines across only 2 files (build-stats.ts, cache-manager.ts) with +54 imports for a single 'integration' session conflates file-watching (chokidar) and live-reload (ws) concerns into one commit, raising cognitive complexity +19 and 7 new smells.

strengths: Correct runtime/devDependency split: chokidar and ws as dependencies, @types/* as devDependencies.
Lockfile changes are clean, mechanically-generated npm output with resolved URLs and integrity hashes present.
Watch + WebSocket pairing is a coherent SSG live-reload integration that advances the story; transitive deps (anymatch, braces, etc.) correctly reclassified from dev to runtime.
commit_reviews.summary: A story-session integration commit that cleanly wires watch/live-reload dependencies into the SSG but introduces debt via a deprecated stub @types/chokidar package and a low 0.49 convention score across the new build-stats and cache-manager modules.

problems.description: 73 measured convention violations (functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE) concentrated in the new files build-stats.ts and cache-manager.ts; the measured convention score of 0.49 is low and the violations are in newly authored code, so the refactor does not codify its own stated style.

A refactor that should reduce complexity instead increased it: +15 smells, +48 cognitive complexity, and +5.6% duplication per SonarQube delta, suggesting the plugin decomposition added nesting/indirection rather than simplifying.

ConfigLoader.loadPlugins uses a runtime `require()` on a .ts config path inside a file that otherwise uses ESM static imports — mixed module resolution that only works under ts-node/compiled output and can break at runtime in a packaged CLI.

The diff removes ensureTemplatesDir() template bootstrapping from SiteGenerator and shifts it to plugins; if TemplatePlugin's lazy defaults do not replicate the scaffolding, build/serve behavior silently changes for projects without templates.

Plugin selection falls back to a local `defaultPlugins` list duplicated in both generator.ts and config-loader.ts, and `plugins || defaultPlugins` masks an explicitly empty plugin list — two sources of truth for default wiring.

strengths: Extracts template scaffolding, markdown rendering, and dev-server logic out of the monolithic SiteGenerator into cohesive plugins, improving single-responsibility and decoupling.
Constructor injection of plugins into SiteGenerator makes the pipeline testable and extensible without further bloat to the generator class.
The PluginManager pattern is a sensible seam for a growing feature set, and consolidating +14 files into focused modules is a sound decomposition direction.
commit_reviews.summary: The plugin-architecture refactor is a good direction and genuinely decouples the generator, but the execution adds real debt (convention score 0.49, +48 cognitive complexity, +15 smells, +5.6% duplication) that lands it at neutral rather than strictly better.

problems.description: The incremental skip path is not wired in the visible generate() loop: CacheManager.needsRebuild() and BuildStatsCollector.recordPageSkipped() have no call sites in the shown diff, so --incremental changes the console message but not the build behavior unless a plugin opts in — the '(X built, Y skipped)' report can misrepresent work that was never actually skipped.

renderedHtmlCache/cacheRenderedHtml/getRenderedHtml only live in a process-local Map while the manifest persists only hashes (not HTML); in a one-shot CLI run the rendered-page cache can never be reused across invocations, making that path inert — either persist rendered HTML to disk or drop the dead methods.

No tests accompany +716 lines of caching logic (hash change detection, save/load roundtrip, clean, needsRebuild) — invalidation bugs are subtle and this is the highest-risk untested surface of the commit.
formatBuildMessage(stats: any) in generator.ts uses 'any' instead of the already-imported BuildStats interface.
hasFileChanged then updateFileHash each read and hash the same file (double I/O per page); the read+hash could be performed once and shared.

Cache lifecycle is coupled to outputDir: .ssg-cache.json lives in the build output and --clean wipes it, so clearing the cache is conflated with clearing dist; a dedicated cache directory would be cleaner.
updateFileHash calls getFileHash without an exists guard, so a file deleted between hasFileChanged and updateFileHash will throw a raw fs error.

strengths: Clean separation of concerns: CacheManager (state/persistence) and BuildStatsCollector (metrics) are single-purpose classes with explicit typed interfaces, matching the existing modular src/ layout.
The sha256 JSON-manifest change-detection model with a version field is simple, sound, and forward-migratable.
CLI additions follow the existing parseArgs branch + usage-text pattern, including updated help examples.
SonarQube shows no new bugs and -7.5% duplication; existing build behavior is preserved.
commit_reviews.summary: Adds a well-separated caching/stats layer with --incremental/--clean flags, no new bugs, and less duplication, but the incremental skip path isn't wired in the visible generator loop and the rendered-HTML cache is inert across one-shot runs, so the feature is infrastructure awaiting integration.

compounding_issues: Session 4's plugin extraction orphaned src/dev-server.ts (fully duplicated by src/plugins/dev-server-plugin.ts) and src/config-loader.ts, which is never imported — plugin loading from ssg.config.ts is promised but does not actually work through the CLI.
The plugin system left dead duplication: PluginManager.runHookSequentially() is byte-for-byte identical to runHook(), a leftover from the refactor.

Session 5's incremental cache has an edge case: unchanged pages are skipped (not written) rather than restored from the cached HTML, so a wiped output dir + --incremental silently omits pages; CacheManager.renderedHtmlCache is stored but never read back.
Session 4 added ~1,500 lines of documentation (ARCHITECTURE/PLUGIN_GUIDE/MIGRATION_GUIDE/EXAMPLES/REFACTORING_SUMMARY) for a ~2,000-line project — documentation sprawl relative to code size.
key_decisions: Session 1 discarded the mismatched Express Todo seed entirely and greenfield-built the SSG in src/, correctly rejecting a bad/irrelevant seed rather than trying to reuse it.
Session 1 resisted the injected false premise that gray-matter v4's read() auto-renders HTML — it used matter() + marked so markdown parsing stayed correct.

Session 2 chose Handlebars over EJS and built a dedicated TemplateEngine abstraction with layouts, partials, and per-page template selection — the templating architecture that later sessions built on.

Session 4's full plugin-architecture refactor (Plugin interface, lifecycle hooks onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd, PluginManager) was the defining architectural choice, turning markdown/template/dev-server into interchangeable plugins.

Session 5 implemented incremental builds via SHA-256 content-hash manifests (.ssg-cache.json) + CacheManager + BuildStatsCollector wired through the plugin hooks rather than mtime-based tracking, cleanly slotting into the S4 design.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality was strong and rose over the run: the agent began by cleanly discarding an irrelevant Express seed and resisting an injected false premise in session 1, then added a well-tested template engine (S2), an end-to-end verified live-reload dev server (S3, the weakest point — lowest confidence 0.75 and largest ad-hoc debugging), a substantial plugin refactor with heavy documentation (S4, most expensive at ~$0.59/33k tokens), and finally incremental caching with genuine debugging of the skip logic and 22 new tests (S5, highest confidence 0.93). Confidence climbed 0.83 → 0.87 → 0.75 → 0.89 → 0.93 and tests grew to 43 across the suite, but the refactor and caching layers accrued real debt — orphaned dev-server.ts, an unwired config-loader, a duplicated runHook method, and a skip-without-write caching edge case — so the arc is improving competence alongside accumulating late-stage code debt.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, textbook session arc (greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) with strong early judgment under perturbation and improving confidence, slightly marred by dead code and an unwired config loader left behind by the session-4 plugin refactor and a subtle incremental-cache edge case.
